package_info.why_malicious: The report does not describe any specific malicious software package or code. Instead, it provides a sector-level threat analysis for the retail sector, detailing attack vectors and threat actor tactics such as credential stuffing, account takeover, inventory scalping, AI/LLM-generated phishing, gift card cracking, fraudulent transaction automation, and web/API scraping. No particular malicious package, code sample, or version is mentioned.

behavioral_signatures: Automated bot traffic performing credential stuffing, account takeover, and inventory scalping, characterized by rapid, repeated login attempts and high-frequency purchase or cart activity.
Phishing emails generated by AI/LLM for initial access, often exhibiting subtle linguistic patterns or contextually relevant lures targeting retail employees or customers.
Gift card cracking and fraudulent transaction automation, evidenced by repeated balance checks and rapid, sequential gift card redemption attempts.
Web/API scraping for pricing and promotion exploitation, observable through high-volume, non-human API requests targeting product, pricing, or promotional endpoints.
network_indicators: Unusual spikes in login attempts from single IPs or IP ranges, especially those associated with known proxy or VPN services.
Automated traffic patterns mimicking consumer behavior, such as rapid cart additions, checkouts, or inventory queries from the same source.
Outbound connections to known botnet command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, as identified by threat intelligence feeds.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor authentication and transaction logs for high-frequency, automated requests indicative of bot activity, such as rapid login attempts, repeated gift card balance checks, or bulk inventory purchases. Apply behavioral analytics to detect AI-generated phishing emails and credential stuffing attacks, including analysis of email content and sender patterns. Track for abnormal API usage and scraping patterns, such as excessive requests to product or pricing endpoints. Employ anomaly detection on transaction and login flows to identify deviations from typical user behavior, and monitor for unusual third-party vendor access or privilege escalation attempts.
